title: Customer data request priority scorer and response runbook for logging/redaction/retention/export
creator: Sofia Alvarez
description: Create a defensible, auditable intake scorer and operational runbook that productizes how we prioritize and respond to enterprise customer requests for logging redaction, retention changes, PII handling, and audit exports. Purpose is to reduce triage time, ensure consistent routing to Security/Legal/Infra/Support, and provide templated customer responses and SLOs.
background: We receive high-variance customer requests that touch logging retention, redaction, PII extraction/exports, and audit data. Current triage is ad hoc across CS, Support, and Solutions Engineering which causes inconsistent SLAs and repeated engineering/context switching. Multiple recent high-effort requests flagged by Sales indicated unclear prioritization and missing decision criteria.
goals: 1) Define a scoring rubric that maps inbound request attributes to priority buckets and routing; 2) Ship a concise runbook and response templates for each bucket; 3) Integrate scoring fields into intake form and initial support play; 4) Training sessions for CS and Solutions.
non_goals: This ticket does not implement backend enforcement (e.g., automated redaction engines) or modify retention config UI. Those are follow-ups owned by Engineering.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Scoring rubric documented and reviewed by Security, Legal, and Support; 2) Runbook with step-by-step routing and SLA targets published in Confluence; 3) Intake form fields updated in Support workflow and validated on 3 trial requests; 4) Two templated customer responses for each priority bucket approved; 5) Minimal 30-min training recorded and shared.
proposed_solution: Design a 7-factor priority scorer (customer type, data sensitivity, regulatory scope, production impact, request complexity, engineering effort estimate, contractual obligation). Each factor scored 0-3; total maps to Priority: P0 (>=16), P1 (12-15), P2 (8-11), P3 (<8). Define mandatory routing rules: P0->Eng+Security+Legal+SRE immediate, P1->Eng+Security queued with SLA, P2->CS/Support+Solutions, P3->Backlog with templated guidance. Publish decision checklist and response templates.
scoring_factors: Data sensitivity: regulated PII/PCI/PHI (3), low-sensitivity logs (0-1)
Regulatory scope: active investigation/compliance deadline (3), advisory (1)
Production impact: business outages or degradation (3), informational (0-1)
Request complexity: requires infra change/DB migration (3), config change only (1)
Engineering effort estimate: >3 sprints (3), 1 sprint (2), <1 sprint (1)
Contractual obligation: SLA/contract clause triggers (3), non-contractual (0)
Scoring mapping: total 0-21 maps to Priority buckets as described in proposed_solution
runbook_summary: Step 0: Intake capture — ensure the intake form flags sensitive fields (PII types, retention window, export formats). Step 1: Apply automated scorer in Support UI (manual fallback allowed). Step 2: Route per priority and notify required stakeholders. Step 3: Initial ack email to customer within SLA window with templated guidance. Step 4: Triage call setup for P0/P1. Step 5: Post-resolution audit and closure note including compliance artifacts.
sla_targets: P0: initial acknowledgement within 1 hour, incident-style response, resolution target 72 hours or documented mitigation
P1: acknowledgment within 4 business hours, triage meeting within 3 business days, resolution target 2-4 weeks depending on effort
P2: acknowledgment within 24 business hours, response plan within 10 business days
P3: acknowledgment within 3 business days, guidance and backlog placement
routing_rules: If contractual obligation >=3 then route to Legal + Account Exec immediately
If data sensitivity >=3 then auto-include Security and Privacy
If production impact >=2 then SRE/On-call is CC'd
If engineering_estimate >=3 then create ENG sub-issue and mark dependency
example_decisions: Case A: Enterprise customer requests 7-year audit export for PII -> scores: customer_type 3, data_sensitivity 3, regulatory_scope 2, production_impact 0, complexity 2, effort 2, contractual 3 => total 15 -> P1. Route to Eng+Legal+Security, schedule export job, provide data-handling attestation template.

Case B: Startup requests log retention increase from 30d to 60d for non-PII -> scores total 6 -> P3. Provide templated instructions for self-serve retention change and place in backlog for product consideration.

Case C: Mid-market customer requests immediate redaction for GDPR erasure -> scores total 18 -> P0. Trigger incident workflow: Eng+Security+Legal, remove artifacts, post-action audit, confirm with customer and update contract folder.
response_templates: P0 initial ack: 'We have classified this as high-priority and have initiated an incident response. A cross-functional team has been notified and will contact you within 1 hour with next steps.'

P1 initial ack: 'Thanks — we've prioritized this and will coordinate a scope review within 3 business days. If this request has contractual or regulatory urgency please reply and indicate the deadline.'
P2/P3 ack: 'Thanks for the request. We've created a ticket and assigned it to our governance queue. We'll provide a proposed plan within 10 business days.'
training_plan: Two 45-minute sessions: 1) Support/CS intake training and scoring demo; 2) Eng/Security/Legal triage playbook review. Recordings uploaded to Confluence. Include a 1-page quick reference card and FAQ.
metrics_and_monitoring: Instrument intake form to capture scorer distribution, time-to-ack, time-to-resolution by priority, and re-open rate. Dashboards to be added to Console under 'Governance Requests' with weekly reports to PM and Head of Support.
tradeoffs_and_open_questions: 1) Granularity vs speed: more factors improve accuracy but slow human raters; plan: implement basic 7-factor scorer with optional advanced fields. 2) Automated enforcement vs manual ops: initial release is human-mediated to avoid false positives. 3) Who owns maintenance of templates? Proposal: PM maintains content; Legal approves changes.
implementation_notes: ENG needs a small API endpoint to accept score payloads and create sub-issues when threshold crossed. Support will add fields to Zendesk form for initial capture. Legal needs review of all customer-facing templates before publish.
